A_target.statement:
In the [[Definition:Simply Typed Lambda Calculus|simply typed $\lambda$-calculus]], there is no closed term $Y$ of type $\paren {T \to T} \to T$ with $Y f =_\beta f \paren {Y f}$ for a variable $f : T \to T$.
In particular there is no typable [[Definition:Fixed-Point Combinator|fixed-point combinator]].

B_source.statement: Every well-typed term of the simply typed $\lambda$-calculus is [[Definition:Strongly Normalizing|strongly normalizing]], and $\beta$-reduction is [[Definition:Confluent Relation|confluent]].

substitutions.an arbitrary well-typed term: Y f with f a free variable

derived.normal forms: a term equal to f applied to itself, which is impossible

object_map.reformulation: Compare the normal forms of Y f and f (Y f): confluence forces them to coincide, but one is strictly larger.

validity_conditions: f must be a variable, so that applying f cannot create a redex.
Recursion therefore has to be added as a primitive, as in PCF.
proof_plan:
Let $f$ be a variable of type $T \to T$, so $Y f$ is well-typed.
By the source result, $Y f$ has a normal form $N$.
As $f$ is a variable, $f \paren {Y f}$ reduces to $f \, N$, which is again normal.
If $Y f =_\beta f \paren {Y f}$, then by confluence the two terms have the same normal form, so $N \equiv f \, N$.
